ety.text: Attested early 14th century, of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Danish ha, Dutch ha, Finnish ha, Hungarian ha, Latin ha, Latvian ha, Swedish ha.

senses.d: An exclamation of triumph or discovery.
A sound of hesitation: er, um.
Said when making a vigorous attack.
ex: Mona: Hee! Ha! Ho! Ha! The brain buffet is closed, buddy! Take that! And this!
"That's well. Well," cried he, now for my turn. Ha! a hit! a hit!"

senses.d: The sum of bodily parts; the physical body.

grp.label: an exclamation of triumph or discovery

ety.text: Inherited from Old French a! (“oh! ah! woe!”), of expressive origin.
